Schmid-Leiman transformation

Source: R/efa_schmid_leiman.R
efa_schmid_leiman.Rd

Transforms an oblique factor solution into a hierarchical solution with one general factor and group factors that are uncorrelated with it and with each other (Schmid & Leiman, 1957). With the same settings, the results agree with psych::schmid() and with the SPSS syntax of Wolff and Preising (2005).

Usage

efa_schmid_leiman(
  x,
  Phi = NULL,
  estimator = c("PAF", "ML", "ULS", "MINRES"),
  g_name = NULL,
  estimate_control = NULL
)

Source

Schmid, J. & Leiman, J. M. (1957). The development of hierarchical factor solutions. Psychometrika, 22(1), 53–61. doi:10.1007/BF02289209

Wolff, H.-G., & Preising, K. (2005). Exploring item and higher order factor structure with the Schmid-Leiman solution: Syntax codes for SPSS and SAS. Behavior Research Methods, 37 , 48–58. doi:10.3758/BF03206397

Mansolf, M., & Reise, S. P. (2016). Exploratory bifactor analysis: The Schmid-Leiman orthogonalization and Jennrich-Bentler analytic rotations. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 51(5), 698–717. doi:10.1080/00273171.2016.1215898

Arguments

x

An oblique efa_fit() or psych::fa() solution, a pattern matrix (give its factor intercorrelations in Phi), or a second-order CFA solution from lavaan.

Phi

matrix. The factor intercorrelations of the pattern matrix in x. With an efa_fit() or psych::fa() solution in x, Phi replaces the fitted factor intercorrelations. Not used for a lavaan solution.

estimator

character. The estimator of the second-order efa_fit(): "PAF" (default), "ML", or "ULS". "MINRES" is a synonym for "ULS". Not used for a lavaan solution and for two first-order factors, for which no second-order EFA is done.

g_name

character. The name of the general factor in a lavaan solution. If NULL (default), the latent variable that loads on the other latent variables is used.

estimate_control

An estimate_control() object with the settings of the second-order efa_fit(). NULL (default) uses the efa_fit() defaults. Not used for a lavaan solution and for two first-order factors.

Value

A list of class c("efa_schmid_leiman", "SL"):

orig_R

The correlation matrix of the input solution. NA for a pattern matrix.

sl

The Schmid-Leiman loadings: the general factor (g), the group factors, the communalities (h2), and the uniquenesses (u2).

L2

The second-order loadings, with one row for each first-order factor.

vars_accounted

The variances explained by the general factor and the group factors.

iter

The number of iterations of the second-order EFA.

convergence

The convergence code of the second-order EFA (0 = converged; see efa_fit()).

settings

The estimator and the estimation settings of the second-order EFA.

iter, convergence, and settings are NA if no second-order EFA was done, that is, for a lavaan solution and for two first-order factors.

Details

The factor intercorrelations are factor analyzed to get one second-order (general) factor. The general-factor loadings of the items are their first-order loadings times the second-order loadings. The group-factor loadings are the first-order loadings times the residual standard deviations of the first-order factors. The general factor and the group factors thus divide the common variance, for example for McDonald's omegas (see efa_reliability()).

The transformation has proportionality constraints: in each group factor, the ratio of the group-factor loading to the general-factor loading is the same for all items. Thus, it recovers a bifactor structure exactly only if each item loads on one group factor and these ratios are equal. If items have cross-loadings, it overestimates their general-factor loadings, and the result depends on the oblique rotation of the first-order solution (Mansolf & Reise, 2016). The orthogonal bifactor rotation of efa_fit() (rotation = "bifactorT") does not have these constraints.

With two first-order factors, the second-order loadings are not identified. The two loadings then get the same absolute value, and their product is the factor intercorrelation, as in psych::schmid().

A lavaan solution must have one second-order factor and no other paths or covariances between the latent variables. Its general-factor loadings also include the direct loadings of the general factor on the items, if the model has them.

The group factors keep the column order and the names of the input solution. If the columns do not have unique names (or a name is "g", "h2", or "u2"), all group factors are labelled "F1" to "Fk".

See also

Other factor rotation: efa_procrustes()

Other reliability coefficients: efa_reliability(), print.efa_reliability()

Examples

efa_mod <- efa_fit(test_models$baseline$cormat, N = 500, n_factors = 3,
                   estimator = "PAF", rotation = "promax")
efa_schmid_leiman(efa_mod)

# A psych::fa() solution, with the psych settings for the second-order EFA
fa_mod <- psych::fa(test_models$baseline$cormat, nfactors = 3, n.obs = 500,
                    fm = "pa", rotate = "Promax")
efa_schmid_leiman(fa_mod, estimate_control = estimate_control(type = "psych"))

# A lavaan second-order CFA solution
if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)) {
  mod <- 'F1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6
          F2 =~ V7 + V8 + V9 + V10 + V11 + V12
          F3 =~ V13 + V14 + V15 + V16 + V17 + V18
          g =~ F1 + F2 + F3'
  fit <- lavaan::cfa(mod, sample.cov = test_models$baseline$cormat,
                     sample.nobs = 500)
  efa_schmid_leiman(fit)
}
